transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Well, I came in because... recently the school district put this new bilingual social-emotional learning rollout on my plate, right on top of my regular teaching load. I mean, I'm still getting through the day, but I just feel so wound up and... discouraged, I guess, in a way that really isn't like me. I've even started putting off my lesson plans and ignoring emails that I used to just handle without a second thought. It's just become a lot.
Did these feelings start after the new school rollout was added to your workload?

Yes, they did. I'd say it was probably within the first month or two after they added that bilingual SEL rollout to my schedule that I started feeling so unlike myself. Before that change, you know, I was managing my usual teaching load and all my other commitments pretty well. It really just started when that extra work got piled on.
Outside of the stress from this new school rollout, do you find yourself worrying excessively about lots of other areas of your life?

No, not really. I mean, my home life and everything else is pretty stable. I don't find myself worrying about... you know, my family or finances or anything like that. It really is just this specific situation at work that's getting to me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

No, I wouldn't say I feel depressed. It's more just... I'm overwhelmed and stressed out about this specific situation at work. I'm not feeling down in the dumps or anything like that, just really wound up about the extra workload.
Because this stress started, have you been acting out or breaking rules in ways that are unusual for you?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I'm a teacher, so I'm pretty much a rule-follower by nature. I haven't been acting out or doing anything reckless or unusual. It's really just that internal feeling of being overwhelmed by the workload, but my actual behavior... you know, I'm still doing what I'm supposed to do.
